messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — auth anomaly: Multiple failed token reuse attempts across edge proxies (region: us-west-2).  rate spike + suspicious Authorization headers. Severity: P2. Paging sara (oncall) @sara :rotating_light:

sara (oncall): on it. joining #incidents and pulling logs now. who saw the initial alert?

dan: I saw it from the edge metrics. ~350 auth rejects in 6m, unusual for this time. sending pcap to thread.

maria: looking at auth logs — some requests include an Authorization header that matches our token format but traces show it came from multiple distinct client_id values. possible replay or leaked header copies.

jack: any customer impact so far? support dashboard shows ~30 blocked requests returned 401 to 5 customers (small percent). opening a support ticket template.

sara (oncall): triage plan: 1) block offending IPs at firewall 2) rotate service tokens that could be affected 3) run grep across recent staging/prod logs for raw Authorization strings 4) prepare customer-facing note. assigning tasks.

dan: blocking three IPs now (10.13.5.22, 54.210.11.9, 3.94.120.8) at edge-nginx. Applied WAF rule id wf-7832.

ops-bot: firewall rule wf-7832 applied to edge-nginx; blocked 3 IPs.

maria: quick findings: two rotated service keys used by older microservice 'replayer' last touched 2024-11-02 — possible leftover debug token. request logs show header pattern: "Authorization: Bearer rwd_live_" followed by 24 chars. I'll start rotating affected service tokens and create short-lived replacements.

sara (oncall): maria please rotate those keys (replayer) and post the replace commands. dan, confirm we can hot-swap without downtime?

dan: replayer runs on Dedicated pool with autoscale; we can push new env var with new token and do zero-downtime restart. deploying to canary first.

maria: rotation steps (running now):
```
# revoke old key (service account: svc-replayer)
redwoodctl secrets revoke --service svc-replayer --key rwd_live_xxx
# create new key and set in k8s secret (one-liner)
redwoodctl secrets create --service svc-replayer --name rwd_live_replace && kubectl set env deploy/replayer TOKEN=$(redwoodctl secrets get rwd_live_replace) -n infra
```
I'll keep keys valid only for 10m after rollout then revoke completely. posting logs when done.

deploy-bot: canary rollout for replayer triggered (deployment replayer v2 -> 10% traffic).

jack: I drafted a short customer message for the affected customers. ETA for dispatch once we confirm token revocation: "We observed some failed authentication attempts affecting a subset of requests. We have blocked suspicious sources and rotated tokens; no customer data was accessed. We'll follow up when rotation is complete." Want product sign-off from emma.

emma: approved, small wording tweak: add timeframe and ask customers to rotate any leaked keys on their side if they used copy/paste tokens.

sara (oncall): hunting for leaked logs: run scan against s3 access logs and staging buckets. dan, any chance logs shipped externally?

dan: we have a forwarded logging pipeline to external indexer (third-party) but ingestion shows no obvious auth header dumps. still scanning. grep job kicked off: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/2026-03-10-logs - | grep -E "Authorization: Bearer rwd_live_" -n`

maria: grep returned matches in a staging debug log file on instance i-09d2f (staging). file contained full headers. looks like debug printing accidentally enabled. I'm pulling file and truncating then rotating staging keys.

ops-bot: key rwd_live_xxx revoked for svc-replayer at 1765432350.

sara (oncall): status update: IPs blocked, svc-replayer rotated, canary healthy. no evidence yet of exfil to third parties. customer notifications drafted and awaiting send. severity remains P2.

jack: sending message to the 5 impacted customers now (support ticket IDs attached).

maria: follow-ups: 1) add a guard to prevent printing Authorization header in debug logs (PR in progress) 2) audit other services for similar debug flags 3) rotate any long-lived keys older than 90 days.

dan: I'm scheduling a cron grep job for next 24h to detect replays, adding ephemeral blocklist for any new IPs that repeat.

emma: putting a short incident note in the customer incident tracker and flagging for post-mortem if we find external exfil.

sara (oncall): handing off to next oncall at 1765432745. next steps for oncall: confirm all revoked keys are unusable, complete support replies, and schedule PM/SEC sync tomorrow. I'll leave the channel but reachable. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
